principles: record software, environment, parameters, methods, inputs, outputs and provenance
automate experiments where practical and preserve raw observations
record random seeds and run-time parameters when randomized scheduling or timing is used
distinguish artifact functionality from independently reproduced results
do not promote blocked setup or absent fault injection to candidate PASS/FAIL

preExecutionAmendments.reason: Prevent mixing code revisions across round-robin repetitions or candidates; operationalizes the existing requirement to record software identity and provenance.
preExecutionAmendments.constraint: The T5/r1 lifecycle qualification support may originate from an earlier verified revision only while its candidate lifecycle-qualification hash remains current; every record admitted to one formal benchmark ledger must otherwise share one verified Git repository revision.

executionOrder.reason: avoid completing all repetitions of one candidate before exposing later candidates to the same experimental window
executionOrder.sequence: for repetition 1..100, execute each critical mutant for each candidate using the declared environment profile; record any unavailable run as BLOCKED rather than substituting another configuration

promotionRules.pass: all predeclared acceptance checks true under executed intended fault
promotionRules.fail: at least one predeclared acceptance check false under executed intended fault
promotionRules.benchmarkEligibility: all six critical mutants must have at least 100 unique valid records and none may be BLOCKED or INCONCLUSIVE
